title: Scintilla statistics: method standard, tools, critique, next studies

rules.rule: Universe without survivorship: point-in-time membership from the whole-market day files; leader sets are percentiles recomputed each month
rules.why: A list of today's winners measured backwards can only show winning

rules.rule: Full distributions, never one cut-off: every percentile 1..100, every depth, every horizon; report the whole curve
rules.why: A cut-off chosen by eye is a test we ran without counting it

rules.rule: Count what is independent: episodes and years, not days; report the effective sample size
rules.why: 275 days deep below the 200-day are five bear markets, not 275 coin flips

rules.rule: Resample runs of days (stationary block bootstrap, block at least the horizon) for every range
rules.why: Overlapping forward windows and clustered episodes make coin-flip ranges too narrow by 3 to 5 times

rules.rule: Count the tests: false-discovery control (Benjamini-Hochberg) over every rung, bucket and rule tried; SPA / Reality Check when rules are searched
rules.why: 100 rungs at a 10% line give 10 winners by luck; 254 rules give 25

rules.rule: Walk-forward: choose on the first half, report the second; both halves shown side by side
rules.why: A rule that only holds where it was found is a description, not a finding

rules.rule: Condition on the market state first (above/below and slope of the 200-day, VIX percentile, breadth); pooled numbers come after
rules.why: Rising tide lifts all boats: most stock outcomes are the market's outcome

rules.rule: Effect size before significance: the shift of the whole outcome distribution against any day, in the instrument's own usual days
rules.why: A tiny, certain edge and a big, uncertain one need different decisions

rules.rule: Outcomes with no lookahead and no truncation: read only from bars up to the entry close; open episodes are censored, not dropped; waits are survival curves
rules.why: 'Every pullback made a new high' is true of any index that went up; the wait is the finding

rules.rule: Report to Alan in three numbers and one word: how many (independent episodes), how sure (90% resampled range against any day), how big (middle shift), and a status word: luck-proof / leaning / a list
rules.why: A non-technical reader needs to know whether to act, watch, or ignore

critique.sound: large pooled sample; corrected report timing in S8
critique.weak: fixed 20-session window; today's 313 names measured backwards (survivors); unweighted by size or era
critique.fix: R1 universe from the day files; window = pivot to report; cap-weight by era

critique.weak: 178 rules, best 64.3% reported without a test-count correction; 1% touch bands and 20-session window are cut-offs
critique.fix: SPA with window-start entry as the benchmark; touch band as a percentile of usual days

critique.sound: corrected itself: shuffled-price control killed the post-report-drop claim; lift table is descriptive
critique.weak: 254 rules, 10 pass both halves at 65%: at a 5% level 254 rules give ~13 false passes per half, so 10 is what luck looks like
critique.fix: SPA / StepM over the 254; report the count that survives; hindsight lows only as description

critique.sound: month-clustered bootstrap, 200-draw shuffle, episodes not days, recency columns, no lookahead percentiles
critique.weak: about 130 fund tests (11 rungs x 4 states x 3 horizons) read against a 1-in-20 line: 6-7 cross it by luck; 20-session horizon fixed; 313 survivors pooled unweighted
critique.fix: FDR over the whole ladder (this page shows the result: 0 rungs survive on SPY); add to-next-swing horizon; R1 universe

critique.sound: pivot rule with sensitivity rows; confirmation dates; bad prints cleaned and listed; questions ranked
critique.weak: depth buckets are cut-offs; next-leg-only outcome (fixed by rsi-ladder); 200-day band: 275 days = ~5 independent, ranges not shown; leader definition proposed but not tested
critique.fix: continuous depth; survival curves; block bootstrap and effective n on the band table; N4 and N5 below

critique.sound: full histories, no-hindsight percentiles, 90% ranges, 'may be luck' wording
critique.weak: 17 instruments x 4 horizons = 68 ranges uncorrected; bullish divergence n=11 on SPY is a list; bottom-10% zone still a cut-off (the ladder fixes it)
critique.fix: FDR over the 68; state 'a list' when n<20 episodes

critique.sound: rungs 1..100; honest note that 207/200 pooled hits mean narrow bands; time-to-new-high curves
critique.weak: '1335 of 1336 made a new high' is a statement about indexes that went up; the wait is the finding; open pullbacks must be censored, not counted as failures or dropped
critique.fix: Kaplan-Meier curves with censoring; FDR over rungs (0 survive on SPY at 20 sessions, this page)

critique.sound: six questions with 90% ranges; counts separate years behind one-year windows; measures Alan's thesis instead of assuming it
critique.weak: equal-weight extremes n=3-9 per pair (a list); 12 months + expiry weeks + Fed days = many tests; block length for 63-session overlapping returns not stated
critique.fix: stationary bootstrap with block >= horizon; FDR across months; pool the 17 pairs into one estimate with a pair effect

critique.sound: expanding own-history percentiles (no window); stress orientation; false-alarm counts are in the design
critique.weak: not yet published; 'turned first' by pivots depends on the 10-bar rule for both series; lead-time offsets need a shuffle control (as S7b did)
critique.fix: publish hit rate AND false-alarm rate at every threshold (N3); shuffle the condition series in blocks as the control

critique.sound: 2020->2026 from N-PORT holdings is point-in-time; share classes merged; quarters chained exactly

studies.name: Sector rotation at three horizons
studies.question: How long does a leading sector stay leading, how do sectors move between rank quintiles / RRG quadrants, and what does a shift in the Hub's cohort-compare bow tie mean historically?
studies.data: 11 SPDR sectors (Dec 1998->) + SMH, SOXX, XBI, KRE, ITB, XOP, IGV; SPY benchmark; weekly and daily closes from the chart API cache
studies.method: RS = ETF/SPY. Horizons 1, 3, 12 months. (a) rank persistence: Spearman of rank(t) vs rank(t+h) at every h from 1 to 52 weeks; (b) transition matrices of rank quintiles and of RRG quadrants at weekly steps, with expected time in each quadrant; (c) RRG reimplemented in Node (z-scored RS over the window +100, momentum = ROC of the ratio z-scored); (d) bow tie: cross-sectional dispersion of 3-month RS across sectors; its own percentile; what SPY and the leaders did after dispersion widened or narrowed
studies.test: shuffle sectors within each date (keeps the market, kills persistence) for the null; stationary bootstrap by week; walk-forward halves 1999-2012 / 2013-2026; FDR over the 52 horizons
studies.decision: whether 'move to another good name with lower risk' should be read from sector rank; how many weeks a leading sector can be trusted; whether a bow-tie shift is a signal or noise
studies.lane: Urth (Fable or Opus, medium) in Node; Python check with statsmodels

studies.name: Rising-tide gauges
studies.question: When the market rises, how many boats does it lift, and at what levels of breadth / market strength does a stock's own setup stop mattering?
studies.data: SPY swings (S9 pivots); every US common stock from the Massive day files (R2, 2003->) via a Fly one-off, else the 313 cached names as a first cut; sector ETFs
studies.method: for every SPY swing: distribution of stock returns over the same swing; share of names up; quantile regression of stock return on SPY return (slopes at the 10th/50th/90th percentiles); pooled R-squared by regime (above/below 200-day, VIX percentile); gauge = percentile of 'share of names above their 50-day' with what SPY did next at every percentile 1..100
studies.test: block bootstrap by swing; walk-forward halves; effect size as the shift of the whole return distribution
studies.decision: dynamic position sizing to market behaviour: at which gauge level to be patient and at which to be aggressive
studies.cost: medium: one Fly one-off over ~5,800 day files, then cheap
studies.lane: Urth reasoning + Node job; coordinator runs the Fly one-off

studies.name: Bottoms as conditions with base rates
studies.question: For each stress gauge (VIX percentile, VIX/VIX3M, put/call, breadth, RSI, distance to the 200-day, credit), at every threshold 1..100: how often did a confirmed low follow, how often was it a false alarm, how long was the lead, and what did all of them together say?
studies.data: the bottoms lane's series (cached); SPY/QQQ/IWM swing lows
studies.method: hit rate and false-alarm rate per threshold (ROC curve), base rate of lows on any day; lead-time distribution; logistic model of 'low within 10 bars' on the gauges, fitted on 2003-2015, scored on 2016-2026; calibration table ('when it said 30%, lows came x% of the time')
studies.test: Brier score against the base rate; block-shuffled gauge series as the null; FDR over thresholds
studies.decision: the level at which to switch from patient to aggressive buying, with its false-alarm cost
studies.lane: Urth in Node; statsmodels Logit for the check

studies.name: Leaders as a point-in-time percentile set
studies.question: Each month, who were the leaders (top 10%, and every percentile, by 6- and 12-month return among liquid US stocks), did they stay leaders, what share of the market's return did they carry, and what did they look like (distance to the 200-day, RSI percentile, sector)?
studies.data: Massive whole-market day files 2003-> (R2) for prices and dollar volume; FMP historical S&P constituents and shares outstanding for caps; SPY N-PORT holdings 2019->
studies.method: monthly cross-section, liquidity floor = dollar volume above the month's 20th percentile; leader = percentile rank of trailing return; persistence = share still in the top decile after 3/6/12 months vs 10% by chance; contribution = weight x return chained by quarter; alphalens tear sheet of the rank as a factor (quantile returns, IC, turnover)
studies.test: Newey-West errors on the monthly series; walk-forward halves; FDR across percentiles
studies.decision: which names count as leaders for every other study; whether to buy leaders on pullbacks or rotate into the next set
studies.cost: medium: the Fly one-off from N2 builds the same universe; then cheap
studies.lane: Urth designs; Node job on Fly; alphalens in Python

studies.name: The 200-day as a pooled fact
studies.question: Is 'deep below the 200-day is a problem' true across a statistically relevant set, and where does the problem begin?
studies.data: SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, 11 sectors, S&P 500 index 1928->, Nasdaq 100 1985->, Russell 2000 1987->, Dow 1985->, EFA/EEM, gold, oil, Bitcoin; the leaders set from N4
studies.method: distance = close/SMA200-1, continuous, and as the instrument's own percentile; outcome distributions (20/60/120/250 sessions and to the next swing high): median, 10th percentile, share with a 10% lower close; every 1% band; 'first close below -X' event study for X = 0..20; slope of the 200-day as the second dimension; pooled across instruments with an instrument effect (hierarchical: each instrument's curve shrinks toward the pooled curve)
studies.test: stationary bootstrap by episode with block >= horizon; effective n reported per band; monotonic-trend test of the lower tail against depth; walk-forward halves; FDR across bands
studies.decision: a risk-cut rule: the depth below which the lower tail rises for the pooled set, stated with its range
studies.lane: Urth in Node; arch/statsmodels check in Python

studies.name: Data-snooping audit of S7 and S7b
studies.question: Of the 178 + 254 entry rules tried, how many beat the window-start entry once the search is counted?
studies.method: export per-report loss series per rule; arch SPA with the window-start entry as benchmark; StepM for which rules; MCS for the set that cannot be told apart
studies.decision: whether any entry trigger before a report deserves a card on the stats tab
studies.cost: cheap; half a day in Python
studies.lane: Urth Python venv locally (no keys needed)

studies.name: Seasonality with real statistics
studies.question: Which calendar effects (month, turn of month, expiry week, Fed days, pre-holiday) survive once all of them are tested together?
studies.data: S&P 500 index 1928-> (cached), FOMC dates, expiry calendar
studies.method: daily return on calendar dummies with HAC errors; effect sizes in usual days; last 30 years separately
studies.test: FDR across all dummies; walk-forward halves
studies.decision: whether the calendar belongs on the stats tab at all

studies.name: Regime states from the data
studies.question: Do two or three market states fall out of SPY returns and VIX on their own, how long do they last, and do the other studies' answers differ by state?
studies.method: MarkovRegression (2-3 states, switching variance) and ruptures PELT on realised volatility; compare the states with the cloud-order states the Station uses
studies.test: expected durations with ranges; out-of-sample filtered (not smoothed) probabilities in the second half
studies.decision: whether the Station's cloud order is a good enough regime label or the studies need a second one
